subject: Conditional failover decision criteria and operational acceptance
messages:
From: Elaine Chu <elaine.chu@centurybank.com>

Subject: Conditional failover criteria — Century Bank follow-up

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the initial DR/BC overview in the RFP response. A few of our ops folks had follow-ups on the conditional failover decision tree and what Redwood would consider an "acceptable" data-lag at activation. In particular: 

- What exact metric(s) do you use to trigger regional failover (node health, queue depth, KV cache miss rate, end-to-end tail latency)?
- We need concrete RTO and RPO commitments for the hosted product (both typical and the exception window when an SLA credit would apply).
- During automatic failover, how is in-flight session state handled? Do you support graceful KV cache transfer or is there possible token duplication/loss for streaming sessions?
- For canary/partial failovers, what % of traffic do you recommend and what rollback time do you guarantee?

Also, please attach any evidence artifacts (runbook snippet, recent rehearsal report, audit-log sample). We want to validate our acceptance criteria before moving to procurement.

Best,
Elaine
Senior IT Risk Manager
Century Bank
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2025-05-11T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Conditional failover criteria — Century Bank follow-up

Hi Elaine — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers below and I have attached a short runbook extract + evidence pack. Attachments: runbook-conditional-failover-v1.docx, Century_Redwood_DR_Evidence_2025.pdf

Summary (operational):
- Primary triggers: 1) sustained inter-region tail latency breach (95th > configured threshold) 2) persistent GPU pool saturation (queue depth > configured window for X mins) 3) automated health checks failing leadership quorum (node-level and model-serving readiness). We also use request error-rate and prefix/KV cache-miss surge as secondary signals.

- RTO / RPO (hosted API): typical RTO to restore routing + warm-standby spin up = 15 minutes (target). RPO for request-level state is nominally zero for stateless inference. For session-oriented workloads (where applications maintain short-lived conversational context in a cache), RPO up to 60 seconds is the operational baseline when relying on KV cache replication across regions. We surface both metrics in the console during rehearsal.

- In-flight sessions & streaming: we attempt graceful termination for streaming requests; if a mid-token region switch occurs, clients will receive an explicit error and can resume the session using conversation state we persist (last committed prompt + response chunk). We avoid duplication by providing idempotency keys for long-running streams; full zero-loss is only guaranteed when customers enable synchronous cross-region replication (configurable). Details and recommendation in the attached runbook.

- Canary policy: default recommended canary = 5% of production traffic for 10 minutes, with automated health gate checks at 2, 5, and 10 minutes. Rollback decision window is immediate after a gate failure; our automated rollback median completion is ~90s from detection to traffic shift back (can extend during noisy networks). We can contract a stricter SLA for rollback time on Dedicated plans.

Evidence included: rehearsal timeline (last 3 months), sanitized audit-log snippet, runbook excerpt showing decision thresholds.

If you want, we can map these to explicit acceptance criteria (pass/fail checks) for your procurement team.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Regards,
Logan Wright
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Elaine Chu <elaine.chu@centurybank.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-05-12T08:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Conditional failover criteria — Century Bank follow-up

Elaine, Logan — quick clarifying notes from an ops perspective: 

- The 60s RPO assumes KV cache replication (async by default). If Century Bank requires sub-5s RPO for session continuity we will need to enable synchronous replication and reserve cross-region bandwidth — that is a Dedicated/Private plan conversation due to cost.
- We can add an explicit SLA exception clause for scheduled maintenance windows and for events caused by customer-managed network issues; these are typical carve-outs.
- For the canary rollback SLA, we can offer a 99th percentile rollback completion time of 3 minutes (contracted) when the customer agrees to a 24x7 on-call rotation with our ops team during the rollout.

Action items: Logan — can you produce a short table for Century listing (Trigger / Measurement / Threshold / Rollback action / Evidence) so they can include it in their acceptance criteria matrix?

-Ben
Head of Reliability
Redwood Inference

Ben / Logan — this is helpful and gets us much closer. A couple follow-ups from Procurement and our Security team: 

1) Please provide a sanitized audit-log extract that shows a recent rehearsal and the time-to-rollback observed. We need evidence aligned to the 3-minute rollback claim.
2) We require a DocuSign agreement for the rehearsal and an explicit rehearsal date (we'd like the first joint run within 30 days of contract signature).

We are OK to accept the 15-minute RTO and 60s RPO as a baseline for the hosted product, provided the evidence pack demonstrates the typical behavior. The Procurement team will add the Dedicated/Private notes as optional upgrades.

Please send the DocuSign link and the sanitized logs.

Thanks,
Elaine
